findings.rule: the landing rule (ORBIT_CHARTS §1 rule 1); P2; OS14 / C43
findings.title: TODAY THE GIZMO IS A POINT: the piece set at it, centred, enters the part beside every wall, rim and protrusion; P2 never does
findings.numbers: today: 41 of 62 library shapes, 1102 of 1596 sweep cells; up to 48 mm into a part (the metric is capped at the piece's own height: 48 for A, 40 for B — "at least the piece's height", not a wall's). P2: 0 library shapes and 0 cells with an entry or an unmarked air gap — none.
findings.note: Far and medium this is the MARKER only (the piece rides the shell); close in the footprint support covers it (F9). The point-vs-body gap is half a piece wide along every wall.

findings.rule: P2 (§2.2 'Steps remain … moved outward by half its width'); S5
findings.title: P2 MOVES EVERY DEPTH STEP HALF A PIECE OFF THE WALL, it does not remove it
findings.numbers: piece A on the library's travels: 132 depth steps matched T↔P; the offset between today's step and P2's: median 21 mm (A's half-sizes 20.65 / 22.5 mm), range 8 – 39 mm. L03: today steps at the walls (91, 150 mm along the travel), P2 at 111 and 130 — the slot's floor a 19 mm band (60 − 41.3).
findings.note: S5's 'real depth under the gizmo' holds only in the central band; the number of steps is unchanged (glided, the named event).

findings.rule: WS10 (heldFoot: the two smallest sizes of the piece's own box); P2 ② / Q3
findings.title: TODAY THE PIECE'S RULER IS ITS TWO SMALLEST SIZES, NOT ITS FOOTPRINT: a flat piece is judged by its thickness, an oblong one fits either way
findings.numbers: piece B (80 x 80, 40 tall) is judged 40 x 80: today its gizmo goes to the floor of every void 40 – 80 wide (channels 60 wide: L05, L06, Q02) and the piece set there enters the rims by up to 30 mm along the whole travel (35 library shapes). The bar (20 x 100) is judged 20 x 20: turned across the 25 x 105 keyed slot today ENTERS 130 places (max 20 mm); P2 as held: 0. The lid of L19 (300 x 20 x 300), read on the map of the tray alone (the lid not yet placed): today 120, P2 120, its seat 120 — today lands it on its seat too (its 300 mm footprint does not enter the 260 mm opening: bridged).
findings.note: The difference is visible far out (the marker) and decides the goal's landing; close in the footprint support corrects the PIECE (not the gizmo).

findings.rule: P2 ① 'nothing to land on'; S6; OS2, OS11; WS4
findings.title: 'NOTHING TO LAND ON' IS ONE CLASS: through holes wider than the piece, gaps between islands, the inside of an L, a U, a ring, under a table, a bridge, round a small part
findings.numbers: 13 library shapes have places where no part is under the footprint at all; today the same places put the gizmo on a plane with nothing under the piece (12 shapes, unmarked); P2 marks them. Sweep: 43 cells (all through voids or wide gaps) marked by P2; today 77 cells with an unmarked air gap.
findings.note: The same geometry, now named: S6's 'closed for the moment' becomes P2's two answers (closed by the rims / nothing to land on). Nothing changes on the glass except the mark.

findings.rule: S10 / the mouth's hold (S18, P4's one exception); C7(a); C41
findings.title: THE MOUTH'S HOLD FIRES WHEREVER A VOID IS CLOSED ACROSS AND OPEN UP THE FACET WITH NO FLOOR — on the TOP CAP too, and along a gap between islands
findings.numbers: designed case (Q02, a channel through, seen from its end): the red going up is held 28 / 0 mm under the lip, not held coming down — path-dependent, as labelled. Not designed: 32 sweep cells (through slots and islands open toward a cap edge, a through strip = a gap between two islands) hold the gizmo ON THE TOP CAP for up to 479 mm of a dy — a dy along the gap keeps the gizmo at its first place for the whole travel. L07 (the same channel open at ONE end, seen from that end): held 0 — the back wall 340 mm behind counts as a floor, so no mouth, no hold, the lip has no event.
findings.note: Whether the visible lip is a 'mouth' depends on a fact 340 mm away (the channel's far end); and the rule built for a side's lip acts on a cap where no tilt hand-over exists. No rule names either case.

findings.rule: the noise family (§2.6: MAP_COPLANAR_M 0.5 mm), R1 (exposed = not glued), D5, S17 / P1; WS15
findings.title: A LAYER THINNER THAN THE COPLANAR TOLERANCE ERASES THE FACE ABOVE IT: the top's real face 'glued' to a downward face up to 0.5 mm below it, D5 drops the cap, the charts lose the pole
findings.numbers: 76 sweep cells (voids stepped 0.3 mm deep: layers of 0.15 mm) end with a VIRTUAL top cap: far out the foot moves up to 256.5 mm and the facet under the gizmo turns 90° (the side band runs to the pole) — both readings (P1 keeps the same contour). 32 more cells (protrusions stepped 1 mm: layers of exactly 0.5 mm, the tolerance itself) keep their cap but read part of the protrusion as a VOID closed across with no floor — a false 'mouth', and the hold on the top (up to 235 mm of a dy). The plane's level is its FIRST face's (stackOf: planes.find(...)), so the order of the parts moves a facet: L42 (a 0.3 mm step) contour Δ 0.3 mm with the order reversed.
findings.note: Cause: a face's coplanarity is tested against the PLANE's first level, not its own, and R1 glues any opposite face of another part within 0.5 mm of that plane — whichever side of it. Triggered by a part thinner than 0.5 mm or two parts overlapping by less than 0.5 mm (a press fit, the 0.3 mm skin). The spec's noise family states the tolerances but not this.

findings.rule: P1 / S17 ('far or medium, a singularity at the surface does not impact the orbit of the piece - camera')
findings.title: EVERY PROTRUSION MOVES THE PIECE AND THE CAMERA FAR OUT BY ITS HEIGHT: the shell is built on the parts' BOX, and a protrusion grows the box
findings.numbers: 612 of 760 protrusion cells move the far foot (both readings identical); the foot's move / the box's growth: 1 – 1 (the remaining 148: 0.3 mm, under the noise). Library: a 0.3 mm step moves it 0.3 mm, a pin 10 x 10 x 40 moves it 40 mm, the knife 85, the overhang slab 100. Voids: 9 cells move it (a void at an edge or corner that removes the box's extreme, or a corner through-void).
findings.note: BETWEEN two assemblies (a shape against its bare twin, u along the facet's normal). Along ONE assembly the far foot is a different measure: F17.

findings.rule: S5 ('the piece shall not go in (it shall continue its orbit)') against the close-in contact (the footprint support today, P2 ⑤) and P5 / S14
findings.title: CLOSE IN, THE PIECE IN CONTACT DROPS INTO EVERY SLOT IT FITS, THEN A DX ACROSS IT IS TRAPPED AT THE FAR WALL — in both readings
findings.numbers: sweep: drops ≥ 5 mm in 367 cells today / 432 P2; travels ending at a wall in 849 / 833 cells — of which voids where the piece first DROPPED IN: 190 / 215, and protrusions (a proud part a wall, his Q1 (b), as intended): 565 / 532. L03 (60 x 60 slot, piece A): reach 54%, 4 travel-ends trapped (P5), 4 drops ≥ 5 mm — the piece goes in, then cannot leave by the orbit (out by the approach, S14).
findings.note: Measured with the piece at contact (d = 0); beyond the shell's offset the piece rides the shell and does not go in (S5 holds far). The trap is P5 working as written; whether a slot crossed close in should capture the piece is not stated anywhere.

findings.rule: P2 ⑤ ('P2 started at the piece REPRODUCES [the footprint support]'); C24 / C43 (a piece over a facet's edge)
findings.title: CLOSE IN, P2 STARTED AT THE PIECE GIVES TODAY'S FOOTPRINT SUPPORT — except where the footprint hangs past the assembly's edge
findings.numbers: 1398 of 1596 cells: the same reach, traps and drops. 198 differ: by position {"edge":80,"corner":62,"inside":30,"pole":26} — e.g. a rebate 37 mm wide (narrower than A) along the block's edge: today the gizmo stays on the plane (bridged), P2 lets the piece land 1 – 40 mm down into it because part of the footprint is over empty space beyond the edge.
findings.note: No rule says whether a landing may have part of the footprint over nothing (beyond the facet's polygon, beyond the box).

findings.rule: C36 / WS23 (no depth ruler between the coplanar 0.5 mm and the glide's 5 mm); the noise family
findings.title: DEPTH STEPS OF 0.5 – 5 MM ARE JUMPS WITH NO EVENT in both readings
findings.numbers: 238 sweep cells (all with a 1 mm step, or a stepped 6 mm profile: 3 mm halves); max 3 mm. L43 (1 mm): 2 jumps on each reading; L44 (6 mm): glided.
findings.note: P2 changes where the step is, not its size; the spec names 'a depth for flush' in the noise family but no event for the band between.

findings.rule: C31 / C37 / WS22 (a floor = a group within 20°, at its centre's level; beyond 20° in no group)
findings.title: ON A SLOPE TODAY'S POINT LANDS THE CENTRE (the uphill half enters); P2 lands the uphill edge. Beyond the 20° merge today's gizmo leaves the floor
findings.numbers: L26: T enters 232 (max 48 mm), air 0 (max 0); P enters 0, air 0; L27: T enters 0 (max 0 mm), air 258 (max 9.4); P enters 0, air 0; L30: T enters 178 (max 38.7 mm), air 0 (max 0); P enters 0, air 0; L31: T enters 0 (max 0 mm), air 93 (max 54.9); P enters 0, air 0; L45: T enters 396 (max 2.9 mm), air 0 (max 0); P enters 0, air 0; L46: T enters 70 (max 48 mm), air 332 (max ∞); P enters 0, air 0
findings.note: L45 (8° gable): today 2.9 mm into the slope everywhere = half-width x tan 8°; L31 (35° ramp): today's gizmo bridged across the ramp, the piece up to 55 mm over it; P2 exact on both.

findings.rule: S22 (exposed = reachable from outside), S24 (nothing unreachable silently), OS3, C12, C25, C26, C27
findings.title: TODAY COUNTS SEALED AND BURIED FACES AS SURFACE; THE FACES THAT ARE NO PLACE ARE THE SAME CLASSES IN BOTH READINGS (undersides, inner walls, walls facing no facet)
findings.numbers: exposure differs on 3 shapes: L09 today 11520 vs S22 9216 cm²; L19 today 5650 vs S22 3252 cm²; L20 today 9769 vs S22 9462 cm². Coverage under 85% of the S22-exposed area: L10 79% (hidden 21%, no facet 0%); L11 78% (hidden 22%, no facet 0%); L18 74% (hidden 25%, no facet 0%); L24 78% (hidden 22%, no facet 0%); L38 59% (hidden 41%, no facet 0%); L45 78% (hidden 22%, no facet 0%); L48 43% (hidden 56%, no facet 0%); L49 81% (hidden 19%, no facet 0%); L50 32% (hidden 68%, no facet 0%); Q08 58% (hidden 42%, no facet 0%). T and P coverage differ by more than 0.5% on: L18 T 74.9% P 74.4%; L26 T 96.8% P 96.1%; L36 T 99% P 98.4%; L39 T 99.6% P 98%; L40 T 97.3% P 96.6%; L41 T 98.3% P 100%; Q02 T 96.8% P 96%; Q04 T 95.1% P 94.3%.
findings.note: L09's 3 mm gap reads 'sealed' at the flood's 4 mm resolution (the same answer as MAP_GROW's closing). P2's coverage is lower than today's where the piece can only rest ON studs or a rim (the base between studs is never touched) and higher where a footprint hangs past an edge (F9).

findings.rule: S21 (every goal reachable), B4 (withdrawal along the entry), C45 (how a piece enters), S13
findings.title: THE WITHDRAWAL TEST FINDS THE BLOCKED GOAL; A GOAL ENTERED SIDEWAYS IS NO LANDING OF ANY PRINCIPLE
findings.numbers: L03: withdrawal clear; landing T 200 · P 200 vs seat 200; L05: withdrawal clear; landing T -100 · P -100 vs seat 120; L18: withdrawal clear; landing T 20 · P 20 vs seat 20; L19: withdrawal clear; landing T 120 · P 120 vs seat 120; L53: withdrawal clear; landing T 210 · P 210 vs seat 210; Q03: withdrawal clear; landing T 200 · P 200 vs seat 200; Q07: BLOCKED by slab@40.3; landing T 320 · P 320 vs seat 200
findings.note: Q07: the peg under the slab is blocked along +y (S21/B4 confirmed: found at the build, not by the player). L05: the block slid in from the channel's open end (+z) — P2 along the front's normal lands at the channel's back wall (−100), 220 mm from the seat (120): a slid entry has no landing; only the approach along +z reaches it, and no rule names that entry.

findings.rule: OS15 (the classes form a continuum); §2.6 (3) persistence; B6 (at a threshold)
findings.title: A CLASS FLIP AT A RULER MOVES THE GIZMO BY THE FEATURE'S WHOLE DEPTH FOR A MILLIMETRE OF WIDTH, in both readings
findings.numbers: sweep, width 0.9 → 1.1 x A (37.2 → 45.4 mm, the same cell otherwise): the reading at the feature's centre flips in 105 of 399 today and 120 of 399 with P2; the largest move 4.9 mm of gizmo per mm of width. Library rulers: L03 slot width at A's 41.3 ±1: T — P —; L03 slot width at A's 45 ±1: T 240→200 (×20) P 240→200 (×20); L03 slot width at B's 80 ±1: T 240→200 (×20) P 240→200 (×20); L03 slot width at B's heldFoot 40 (its height) ±1: T — P —; L08 groove width at the joint ruler 3.2 (2 x MAP_GROW) ±1: T — P —; L30 ramp angle at the merge 20° ±1: T 209→240 (×15.5) P 216.1→213.4 (×1.3); L43 step height at the coplanar 0.5 mm ±0.2: T — P —; L43 step height at the glide's 5 mm ±1: T 244→246 (×1) P 244→246 (×1); L53 slot length at the bar's 100 ±1: T — P 240→210 (×15).
findings.note: Inherent to any ruler; P2 moves the ruler to the true footprint as held (L03 at 41.3: no flip for P2 since 45 binds; B at its heldFoot 40: no flip either reading — B's ruler is 80 for P2, 80 for today too since its second size binds). The margin to a ruler is what B6 would paint.

findings.rule: P4; S12 / S19 (a function of the placed set, not of the order); WS15
findings.title: P2 IS EXACTLY INVARIANT; TODAY'S DEPTH IS TOO, BUT FOR TIES EXACTLY OVER A WALL AND THE PLANE'S FIRST-FACE LEVEL
findings.numbers: travels 0.37 mm off the walls' exact places: today differs on 1 shapes (L42), P2 on 0. On the travels as drawn (samples exactly over a wall) today's level differs after a quarter turn on 4 shapes (L17, L20, L47, Q09): a point read exactly over a wall takes either level by the rounding (measure zero).
findings.note: The order dependence is F6's cause (the plane's level is its first face's).

findings.title: NOTHING PLACED AND ONE SMALL PART HAVE NO RULE: no box, no map; round a part smaller than the piece every place but its top is 'nothing to land on'
findings.numbers: L51: no map at all (the gizmo held or at the boot centre). L52 (a 30 mm cube, piece A): P2 marks 96 of 242 places nothing to land on; today the gizmo sits on the facets' planes with no part under the piece at 96 places.

findings.rule: P1 / S17 along a travel ('a singularity at the surface does not impact the orbit of the piece - camera'); the shell (orbit_shell.ts)
findings.title: ALONG ONE ASSEMBLY THE FAR FOOT BUMPS AT EVERY DEPTH STEP WHEN THE ORBIT'S DIRECTION IS OBLIQUE: by the step's depth × tan(the direction's angle off the normal)
findings.numbers: the far foot (d = 0.3 m, shellAnchor as the game calls it) along the 1 mm travels with u tilted 20° / 45° off the facet's normal toward the travel. Sweep (piece A): cells with a bump > 0.5 mm at 20° — today 684 (voids 228, protrusions 456), P2 673 (voids 258, protrusions 415); by depth (max at 20° / 45°, cells bumping at 20°, T · P): 0.3 mm: T 0.1 / 0.3 (0) · P 0.1 / 0.3 (0); 1 mm: T 116.8 / 116.5 (32) · P 0.4 / 1 (0); 6 mm: T 2.2 / 6 (310) · P 2.2 / 6 (316); 40 mm: T 14.6 / 40 (342) · P 14.6 / 40 (357) — depth × tan 20° = 0.36 h, × tan 45° = h; today's 1 mm outliers (116.8 mm) are F6's false-mouth cells: the HELD place released, not a depth step. Library, piece A, max bump at 20° / 45° (mm): L03 T 14.6 / 40 · P 14.6 / 40; L12 T 82.1 / 171.3 · P 82 / 173; L35 T 14.6 / 39.9 · P 14.6 / 39; L42 T 0.1 / 0.1 · P 0.1 / 0.1; L43 T 0.4 / 0.7 · P 0.4 / 0.6; L44 T 2.2 / 5 · P 2.2 / 4.7. 40 library shapes bump at 20°.
findings.note: With u along the normal (the calm's full share, a face's middle) the bump is zero by construction; the calm leaves u oblique toward a face's edges, where the shell no longer absorbs a depth step: the foot slides along u by depth × tan(angle). The study's earlier claim 'no bump along one assembly' rested on u = the normal only.
